name: CRIS-IoMT healthcare cloud-control mapping
scope: Azure-first cloud-connected healthcare IoT and Internet of Medical Things assurance research mapping.
certification_boundary: This mapping supports evidence-informed readiness and research evaluation only. It is not NHS DSPT certification, NCSC CAF certification, medical-device certification, or clinical safety approval.
mapping_precision_note: Each control records the cloud evidence used, the assurance claim it can support, the evidence limitation that remains, and the exact expert-review question to preserve the boundary between cloud governance evidence and healthcare assurance.

controls.title: Cloud device-identity registration posture
manual_or_external_evidence: clinical device ownership and lifecycle process

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Identity verification, authentication and authorisation
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Cloud-registered IoMT device identities and authentication metadata contribute candidate evidence toward device and system access governance for cloud-connected healthcare IoT services.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Azure IoT Hub device identity inventory and authentication metadata can support a cloud-side registration and device-access governance claim.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not validate device-side credential storage, firmware trust anchors, biomedical asset ownership, or whether a registered identity maps to an authorised clinical device.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is device identity inventory a meaningful healthcare IoT assurance signal when explicitly bounded to cloud registration and authentication metadata?

controls.title: Shared access policy and key exposure risk
manual_or_external_evidence: application usage of shared access policies

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Identity verification, authentication and authorisation
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Shared access policies determine non-human and application-level authority over IoT ingestion and device management paths.

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Secure configuration
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Least-privilege shared access policies are part of secure cloud configuration for healthcare IoT ingestion services.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: IoT Hub shared access policy names, counts, and rights can support a least-privilege cloud access governance claim.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove how applications use keys, whether secrets are rotated in practice, or whether emergency access procedures are clinically approved.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Are overbroad shared access policies a valid healthcare IoT governance risk when framed as non-human/application authority over ingestion and device-management paths?

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Monitoring coverage
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: IoT Hub diagnostics provide cloud-side logs and metrics needed for healthcare IoT investigation and monitoring coverage.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Diagnostic settings and destinations can support a cloud-side logging coverage claim for IoT Hub telemetry and operations.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove that logs are reviewed by a SOC, retained under an approved clinical investigation policy, or correlated with device-side telemetry.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is diagnostic setting coverage sufficient evidence for a cloud governance monitoring control, subject to separate operational review?

controls.title: IoT security monitoring and Defender coverage
azure_evidence: Defender for IoT coverage where accessible

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Monitoring coverage
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Defender for IoT or equivalent monitoring observability supports security monitoring coverage claims, subject to licensing and tenant permissions.

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Proactive security event discovery
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: IoT-specific security alerts can support proactive discovery where the service is licensed and observable.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Observable Defender for IoT, Defender for Cloud, or equivalent alert integration can support a cloud-side security monitoring evidence claim.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: When licensing, permissions, or service availability prevent observation, the finding is an evidence gap rather than proof that compensating monitoring is absent.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is it defensible to report unavailable Defender/equivalent monitoring evidence as an observability gap rather than a definitive monitoring failure?

controls.title: Public network exposure of IoT ingestion endpoints

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Secure by design
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Public IoT ingestion exposure affects the secure design boundary for healthcare IoT cloud services.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: IoT Hub public network access, firewall rules, allowed IP ranges, and private endpoint state can support a cloud boundary exposure claim.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove whether public connectivity is clinically justified, protected by external controls, or required for remote-care workflows.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is public IoT ingestion exposure a valid healthcare IoT risk signal when intentional-public and remote-care exceptions are handled by manual review?

controls.title: Conditional private endpoint and network isolation posture

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Secure by design
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Private endpoint coverage contributes to the secure architecture of sensitive healthcare IoT telemetry paths.

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Resilient networks and systems
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Network isolation and private connectivity support resilience and segmentation for IoMT services.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Private endpoint inventory and network isolation settings contribute candidate evidence toward sensitive telemetry path isolation, especially when public ingestion lacks compensating IP-filter or certificate evidence.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove end-to-end clinical network segmentation, gateway hardening, or whether public managed ingestion is an accepted design exception.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: For cloud-connected healthcare IoT, when should private endpoint absence be treated as a risk versus an accepted architecture decision?

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Secure data management
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Telemetry routing and retention posture contributes to cloud-side healthcare IoT data governance.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: IoT Hub message routes and governed storage destinations contribute candidate evidence toward cloud-side telemetry routing and retention governance.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove lawful basis, clinical record status, retention-period adequacy, privacy impact assessment approval, or patient-data minimisation.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is telemetry routing to governed storage a useful assurance signal if privacy and clinical-record interpretation are kept outside cloud automation?

controls.title: Key Vault and secret management for IoT integrations
azure_evidence: secret and key metadata where available

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Identity verification, authentication and authorisation
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Secret governance affects automated access paths used by IoT integrations and backend services.

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Secure data management
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Managed key and secret posture supports protection of healthcare IoT telemetry and integration credentials.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Key Vault and secret-management posture can support a cloud-side credential governance claim for IoT integrations.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove which applications consume each secret, whether rotation is operationally followed, or whether third-party supplier secrets are managed outside Azure.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is Key Vault/managed-secret posture a credible proxy for IoT integration credential governance when application usage remains manually validated?

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Monitoring coverage
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Azure Monitor alert rules provide direct cloud evidence of operational monitoring for IoT Hub telemetry conditions.

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Response plan
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Alert routing supports incident response activation, but clinical escalation paths require operational evidence.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Azure Monitor alert rules and action groups can support an operational alerting coverage claim for IoT Hub telemetry conditions.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not prove clinical escalation ownership, incident response quality, alert fatigue, or whether alerts are acted on by accountable responders.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Is a deployed IoT-specific Azure Monitor alert a sufficient cloud-side signal for incident detection readiness, subject to clinical response validation?

controls.title: Evidence sufficiency and clinical safety boundary

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Risk management process
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Clinical-operational ownership boundaries are part of the organisational risk process for healthcare IoT services.

nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.name: Response plan
nhs_dspt_outcome_candidates.rationale: Clinical ownership and escalation responsibility must be documented for incident response involving IoMT services.

mapping_review.cloud_supported_claim: Evidence class counts, unavailable signal counts, and report caveats can support an explicit assurance-boundary claim.
mapping_review.evidence_limitation: It does not replace clinical safety cases, medical-device safety review, biomedical engineering validation, or operational acceptance.
mapping_review.expert_review_question: Does the explicit boundary control make the paper more defensible by preventing cloud evidence from being misread as clinical or medical-device assurance?
